target.title: improve(google): identify OpenClaw Gemini API traffic
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a provider-integration gap where OpenClaw Gemini API traffic was not identified with Google's documented partner/library attribution header. This makes OpenClaw-originated Gemini API key traffic distinguishable without changing authentication behavior.

AI-assisted: yes, implemented with Codex and reviewed locally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google's Gemini API partner integration guidance asks partner and library integrations to send `x-goog-api-client` using a product/version token. This change promotes Google to OpenClaw's documented provider-attribution policy and threads `x-goog-api-client: openclaw/<version>` through direct Gemini REST, OpenAI-compatible/shared policy, GenAI SDK, embeddings, web search, video fallback, and prompt-cache paths.

Auth selection is intentionally unchanged: API key calls still use `x-goog-api-key`, OAuth-style calls still use `Authorization: Bearer`, and the new header is added alongside existing auth headers.

## User Impact

Operators and maintainers can expect OpenClaw Gemini API traffic to be attributed as OpenClaw per Google's partner guidance. No user configuration changes are required.

## Evidence

- `pnpm vitest src/agents/provider-attribution.test.ts extensions/google/api.test.ts extensions/google/transport-stream.test.ts extensions/google/web-search-provider.test.ts extensions/google/google-genai-runtime.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/google-prompt-cache.test.ts`: 8 files, 212 tests passed.
- `pnpm test:extension google`: 29 files, 403 tests passed.
- `pnpm vitest src/agents/provider-attribution.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/google-prompt-cache.test.ts`: 4 files, 90 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: passed.
- `pnpm check:test-types`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
